name: Californium

discovery.discoverer: Glenn T. Seaborg and team, University of California, Berkeley

occurrence: Does not occur naturally; produced artificially in nuclear reactors, though only in extremely small quantities worldwide.
majorUses: Portable neutron source for oil-well logging and detecting metals/explosives
Starting neutron source to initiate some nuclear reactors
safetyNotes: Intensely radioactive, and one of the most expensive substances on Earth by weight — produced in only milligram quantities globally per year.
notableCharacteristics: One of the very few elements whose neutron-emission properties make it directly useful as a compact, portable neutron source, despite its extreme rarity and cost.
ncertRelevance: practical neutron-source applications despite extreme rarity
whyHere: Californium-252 undergoes spontaneous fission at a notably higher rate than most heavy elements, continuously releasing a steady stream of neutrons without needing an external trigger — exactly the property that makes it useful as a compact neutron source despite being made in only milligram quantities worldwide.
didYouKnow: Californium is so scarce and hard to make that a single gram has, at times, been priced at tens of millions of dollars, making it one of the most expensive materials ever produced by humans.
genZNote: One of the most expensive substances humans have ever made, gram for gram. Also doubles as a portable neutron gun for oil rigs.
